From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Fields <jf@brighthealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Metric ownership lattice & QBR prep: May dashboard pass

Team — attaching the May KPI packet (v2). I ran a quick pass on the rolling 28d windows for our four primary signals: median p95 latency (ms), cost per 1M tokens (USD), platform uptime (%), and active usage (monthly active apps). High level findings: 

- Latency: p95 down 7% vs Apr; cause appears to be backend routing rule adjustments on 2027-05-02. Need an owner to confirm kernel selection change.
- Cost: raw cost down 4% but unit cost (1M tokens) is +6% due to a spike in long-sequence workloads from a partner test.
- Uptime: 99.94% — one 40-minute partial outage on 2027-04-28 due to autoscaler misconfig.
- Usage: MAUs +12% with steady per-app request sizes; growth concentrated in US-east.

Ask before I lock this for the QBR deck (deadline Mon 5/10 EOD):
1) Please assign primary owners for each signal (owner + backup).
2) Verify any data caveats — especially the cost spike attribution and whether BrightHealth's integration is in scope.
3) Add any ops playbook links we should surface (latency spike, cache invalidation, fallback model policies).

Attachments: KPI_May2027_dashboard_v2.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)

Thanks — I want this to be cleaned and owner-assigned before the leadership prep call on Wed.

--
Michael Grant
Director, Platform Insights
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Metric ownership lattice & QBR prep: May dashboard pass

Thanks Michael — quick reads from me: 

- I can own Latency (primary) — Aditya will be backup. We'll validate the kernel routing change on 5/02 and confirm whether it fully accounts for the p95 shift.
- I'll note in the deck that we observed reduced variance in tail latencies for short-sequence workloads.

On Cost: I pulled the billing rollup and the spike does line up with a partner test window. Attached a CSV with usage slices; recommend we annotate unit-cost with a "partner test" flag so the QBR doesn't conflate it with baseline unit economics.

Attachment: cost_variance_may2027.csv (CSV, 1 file)

Also — Jordan from BrightHealth is CC'd. Jordan, can you confirm whether your team ran a long-sequence batch job on 2027-05-03 that might have contributed? If so, we can add a note to the QBR and propose a rate-limit guard for partner test windows.

Laura
VP, Product Operations
